reasons: The file is long and dense, and no test is visible.
The canvas context is assumed to exist, with no check for a missing one.

terms.meaning: The object that lets code paint shapes on a canvas.
The imagined viewpoint from which the 3D scene is seen and drawn.
The tilt of the camera up or down.
Smoothing a value so it speeds up and slows down rather than jumping.
Checking which drawn item lies under the pointer.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the data shapes
sections.what: Brings in the tile decoder and the run record and phase types from the shared data file.
sections.why: Likely reason: the engine must read the same record shape the component receives.
sections.watch_out: The engine depends on those shapes staying the same.

sections.name: PHASES, PhaseProgress
sections.title: The list of phases
sections.what: Lists the five phases in order and describes the camera story they make up: rings from above, a stacked cylinder, a close pass, a cluster of surviving datapoints, and a tree down to slides and projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: the order of phases decides how the camera and tiles move.
sections.watch_out: The phase order is assumed in several places, so reordering it needs changes throughout the file.

sections.name: FieldHover
sections.title: What the pointer can hover over
sections.what: Defines the three possible hover results: a project, a slide or nothing, with a screen position.
sections.why: Likely reason: the component needs one simple type to show the right panel.

sections.name: RGB, CAT
sections.title: Colours for the drawing
sections.what: Holds the colours used for the rings, tiles, labels and panels, plus a short list of the four category colours. A comment says these are kept here because canvas cannot read the page's style variables cheaply.
sections.why: Stated in the code: canvas cannot read the page's style variables cheaply.
sections.watch_out: These colours duplicate the page's style values and must be kept in step with them by hand.

sections.name: PALETTE, DEPTH_LEVELS, rgba, clamp01, ease, lerp, hash, Cam, PITCH
sections.title: Palette and small maths helpers
sections.what: Builds the full colour palette, with a set of brightness levels for depth, and provides helpers for clamping, smooth easing, linear blending, a repeatable random-looking number per index, the camera shape and the camera tilt for each phase.
sections.why: Likely reason: precomputing colour strings and using repeatable random values keep each frame cheap and the layout the same from one view to the next.
sections.watch_out: The hash-based values are deterministic, so changing its inputs changes every tile's position.

sections.name: FieldEngine (part 1)
sections.title: Engine setup and basic controls
sections.what: Declares the engine's stored data, including tile arrays, camera, rings and hover state. Its setup records the canvas and reduced-motion setting, sizes the canvas and starts the frame loop. Also provides destroy, visibility, resize and pointer controls.
sections.why: Likely reason: all drawing state must sit in one object so each frame can read it.
sections.watch_out: The frame loop only stops when destroy is called, so the component must call it when it unmounts.

sections.name: FieldEngine: if
sections.title: Setting the record and progress
sections.what: Accepts new progress numbers and skips fly-in animation when jumping or when reduced motion is on. Accepts a new record, recalculates layout when needed, and keeps reveal state if the same run is loaded again.
sections.why: Likely reason: jumping straight to a finished view should not replay the animation, and a refreshed record should not reset what was already revealed.
sections.watch_out: Sameness is judged only by run identifier and tile counts, so a changed record with the same counts keeps its old reveal state.

sections.name: FieldEngine: for
sections.title: Layout: placing tiles in each position
sections.what: Works out where each tile sits in the flat rings, the stacked cylinder, its starting point for the fly-in, and the cluster of used datapoints arranged evenly with the golden angle. Also finds an anchor point for each project.
sections.why: Likely reason: the camera story needs each tile to have one resting place per phase, and the golden angle spreads the cluster evenly.
sections.watch_out: Tile positions depend on the order of projects and tiles in the record, so a reordered record gives a different picture.

sections.name: FieldEngine (part 4)
sections.title: Layout: slide tree and projection
sections.what: Places the slide cards in rows near the bottom, orders the project nodes by the average position of the slides they cite, and stacks each project's used tiles above its node up to 36. It also sets the bounds the camera uses and converts 3D points to screen points.
sections.why: Likely reason: ordering project nodes by their slides' average position keeps the connecting lines from crossing too much.
sections.watch_out: Only 36 tiles are shown per project in the tree and only 36 projects are used in it, so projects beyond those limits are left out of the tree.

sections.name: FieldEngine: target
sections.title: Camera framing and frame loop
sections.what: Works out the camera tilt, distance and height that frame each phase. Each frame it checks visibility, measures elapsed time, eases the camera toward its target, and either turns the view slowly or snaps it to the front at the end. The frame then starts drawing the background and ring guides.
sections.why: Likely reason: each phase needs its own framing so the viewer sees the relevant part of the picture.
sections.watch_out: The frame loop returns early when the canvas is hidden, so the picture stays frozen until it is visible again.

sections.name: FieldEngine: for
sections.title: Drawing the tiles
sections.what: Draws the ring guides and then places every tile for the current progress. Tiles appear when their turn comes, fly in with easing, get coloured by category and state, and gather into the cluster or tree in the later phases. Tiles are grouped by colour and depth for drawing.
sections.why: Likely reason: grouping tiles by colour and depth avoids changing the drawing style for each tile.
sections.watch_out: The rank values decide the order tiles appear, so changing those values changes the sequence of the whole animation.

sections.name: FieldEngine: for
sections.title: Drawing the tiles, labels and halo
sections.what: Draws each colour group of tiles, adds a light outline to every tile of the hovered project, writes the country code and count beside each ring, and adds a soft glow around the cluster during the compute phase.
sections.why: Likely reason: the outline and labels help the viewer link a project to its tiles and its country.
sections.watch_out: Ring labels are placed at fixed angles, so a country with a crowded area may have its label hidden behind tiles.

sections.name: FieldEngine: if
sections.title: Drawing the slide tree
sections.what: In the compose phase, draws the slide cards with simple placeholder lines, the curved lines from each project node up to its slides, and the dots for the project nodes. Afterwards it runs the hover check.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tree shows which projects each slide cites, which the final picture is meant to explain.
sections.watch_out: The card placeholder lines are drawn, not real text, so the slides are a schematic and not a preview of the actual slide content.

sections.name: FieldEngine (part 9)
sections.title: Hover detection
sections.what: Checks the pointer against the slide cards first, then the project nodes, then the nearest tile within a small distance. It reports the result to the component only when it changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: checking the biggest targets first makes hover feel predictable.
sections.watch_out: Hover uses positions from the last drawn frame, so it can trail the pointer by a moment.

summary: The drawing engine that paints the animated collation field on a canvas, moving datapoint tiles through the phases while the camera follows them.
purpose: Turns a run record into a three-dimensional scene shown flat on screen, frames the camera for each phase, and reports what the pointer is over.
why: Likely reason: the file header describes a camera story that needs a lot of drawing logic, which is kept apart from the page component.
how: 1. Lays out every tile in several positions: flat rings, stacked cylinders, a cluster and a slide tree. 2. Chooses a camera framing for the current phase. 3. Each frame, eases the camera and moves tiles toward their targets. 4. Draws rings, tiles, labels, the halo, slide cards and connecting lines. 5. Works out what the pointer is over and reports it.
inputs: A canvas element, a reduced-motion flag, the run record, progress numbers for each phase, and the pointer position.
outputs: Pixels on the canvas, and a hover callback that reports a project, a slide or nothing.
risks: Draws every datapoint on every frame, so large runs can be heavy. Layout is recalculated whenever the record changes.
debug: Blank canvas: check that a model is set and that the canvas has a size. Tiles in the wrong place: check the phase progress numbers. Hover does nothing: check the pointer handoff and the hit test. Slow drawing: count the tiles and look at the frame loop. Motion will not stop: check the reduced-motion flag.
